answer: A nebula-anchored crystal vault stops one operator minting fake peers. First, each applicant locks a crystal deposit, released after peers verify three contributions. Second, the vault maps each deposit to one nebula of activity, so duplicate trails collapse into one identity. Third, neighbours earn nectar only if attestations survive a challenge; false witnesses forfeit part of the deposit. Forging 100 fakes would need $48,000, 300 devices, and six weeks, while an honest peer pays one deposit. Like a beekeeper who knows each hive by its honey, the network trusts history it can taste.
